name: Plumb the Forbidden
oracle_text:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice one or more creatures. When you do, copy this spell for each creature sacrificed this way.
You draw a card and lose 1 life.
blocked_sentences: As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice one or more creatures. When you do, copy this spell for each creature sacrificed this way.

needs.what: A ceiling on a *repeatable non-mana* additional cost that counts how many times the cost can actually be paid, rather than whether it can be paid once. `_additional_ceiling` (src/automtg/engine/legality.py:647) must ask the payment pool for its size when the repeated cost has no mana half -- for `sacrifice`, `min(MAX_ADDITIONAL_TIMES, len(_sacrifice_pool(...)))` -- so that a board with two creatures is offered two paying lines and not six. Paired with it, `pay` must fail closed: the `sacrifice` branch in src/automtg/engine/costs.py:674 has to return False when the pool cannot cover the count, instead of quietly paying nothing.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `additional_cost` + `additional_optional` + `additional_repeatable` compile and run, and for payments the board can afford they are exactly right: paying once sacrifices one creature and makes one copy, paying twice sacrifices two and makes two, and paying zero sacrifices nothing and makes no copy -- all verified in a real game. The defect is entirely above that ceiling. `_additional_ceiling` runs `can_pay` **once** and then returns `MAX_ADDITIONAL_TIMES` (6) for any repeatable cost, leaving the per-line affordability to the price; and the price is computed at src/automtg/engine/legality.py:791 as `cost.plus(card.additional_cost.mana.scaled(additional_times))`. Replicate survives this because its additional cost *is* mana, so `scaled(n)` makes each line dearer and the solver drops the ones the board cannot pay -- which is why `test_the_mana_is_really_charged` passes and nothing has ever caught this. A sacrifice cost has an empty `mana`, so `scaled(n)` is empty and every line 1..6 is priced at the printed {1}{B} and offered no matter how many creatures exist. Taking one of the over-offered lines then pays nothing for the surplus rather than failing: `ask_objects` returns `[]` for an empty pool (src/automtg/engine/effects/context.py:90), the `sacrifice` branch of `pay` sacrifices that empty list and falls through to a True return, and src/automtg/engine/game.py:398 records `obj.cast_additional = action.additional_times` -- the count *requested*, not the count *paid*. The `if not ok` guard at game.py:396 carries `# pragma: no cover - legality already proved payability`, and that premise is false here: legality proved one payment, not six. Measured: with a single creature on the battlefield the engine offers a `Cast Plumb the Forbidden (+6 additional)` line, and taking it sacrifices that one creature, sets `cast_additional = 6`, and resolves seven copies -- seven cards drawn and seven life lost for {1}{B} and one creature. There is no authoring-side way around it. Dropping `additional_repeatable` turns the card into casualty ("sacrifice *a* creature"), which is the approximation the DSL notes forbid; and `sacrifice`'s `count` is a fixed number baked into the selector, so it cannot express "as many as the player chose" either.

needs.what: `{"additional_paid": true}` must read back the number of payments that were actually *made*, so "for each creature sacrificed this way" counts creatures that really died. Today it reads `obj.cast_additional`, which src/automtg/engine/game.py:398 sets to the number of payments requested, unconditionally and after the payment loop.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The value plumbing itself is sound and ships -- src/automtg/engine/effects/values.py:160 reads it off the object being cast, which is what a `spell_cast` trigger sourced to the spell sees, and `copy_spell`'s `amount` consumes it correctly. What is missing is that nothing decrements it when a payment consumed nothing. For replicate the two numbers cannot diverge, because an unaffordable mana payment is never offered; for a repeatable sacrifice they diverge exactly as soon as the board runs out of creatures, and the divergence is the free copies. Fixing the ceiling alone would close the hole for a board that does not change mid-cast, but the count should still be the count paid rather than the count asked for, so a creature that leaves between legality and payment cannot reopen it.

notes:
This record supersedes an earlier one that claimed `additional-cost` and `reflexive-trigger` were missing outright. They are not: both shipped with casualty and replicate, and the card below compiles and passes all six gates.

  card: additional_cost {sacrifice: {controller: you, types: [Creature]}},
        additional_optional + additional_repeatable, a `spell_cast` trigger with
        active_zones ["stack"] and condition additional_paid >= 1 firing
        {op: copy_spell, amount: {additional_paid: true}}, and spell_effects of
        draw 1 + lose_life 1.

It is withheld only because of the ceiling defect above. Gate 5 cannot see it: `find_play` (src/automtg/cards/authoring/verify.py:211) filters cast actions by `kicked` and `second_face` but not by `additional_times`, and legality builds the plain variant before the additional-cost variants, so the harness always takes the zero-sacrifice line and only ever measures "paid nothing". Driven by hand in the verifier's own sandbox (30 lands, 2 creatures, 2 cards in graveyard, 40 life):

  paid 0x -- 0 sacrificed, 0 copies, drew 1, lost 1 life, battlefield 32.  correct
  paid 1x -- 1 sacrificed, 1 copy,   drew 2, lost 2 life, battlefield 31.  correct
  paid 2x -- 2 sacrificed, 2 copies, drew 3, lost 3 life, battlefield 30.  correct
  paid 3x -- 2 sacrificed, 3 copies, drew 4, lost 4 life, battlefield 30.  WRONG
  paid 6x -- 2 sacrificed, 6 copies, drew 7, lost 7 life, battlefield 30.  WRONG

The mechanic is right up to the number of creatures on the board and free above it. Once the ceiling counts the pool and `pay` fails closed, this card should need no new vocabulary -- re-run it as written above.

The same hole is open for any repeatable additional cost whose payment is not mana, so a regression test should cover a repeatable `sacrifice` rather than only replicate's `mana`; tests/unit/test_additional_cost.py::TestReplicate exercises the mana form exclusively, which is why this survived. Deadly Dispute and casualty are unaffected: neither is repeatable, so `_additional_ceiling` returns 1 and the single `can_pay` it performs is the whole truth.
